answer:
## Two-role answer

**Project Lead / Project Manager** and **Data Scientist** are the two roles with the highest proportion of respondents indicating association with requirements/ML aspects in ML-enabled systems. Under the approved primary spec they are **51.03%** and **48.97%** — i.e. the ~49.6% figure in the task corresponds to **Data Scientist**, and the ~61% figure to **Project Lead / Project Manager** (which I measure at 51.03%, see limitations).

## 1. Primary spec (n = 194 respondents with a valid Q8 block; association := "quoted")
Bootstrap: whole 8-role respondent vector resampled, B = 20,000, seed = 20241025, percentile 95% CI.

| # | role | k/n | pct | bootstrap 95% CI | Wilson | BCa | SE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Project Lead / Project Manager | 99/194 | **51.031** | [43.814, 58.247] | [44.045, 57.977] | [43.299, 57.732] | 3.626 |
| 2 | Data Scientist | 95/194 | **48.969** | [41.753, 56.186] | [42.023, 55.955] | [41.237, 55.670] | 3.577 |
| 3 | Business Analyst | 50/194 | 25.773 | [19.588, 31.959] | [20.131, 32.356] | [19.588, 31.959] | 3.162 |
| 4 | Developer | 37/194 | 19.072 | [13.918, 24.742] | [14.165, 25.180] | [13.402, 24.742] | 2.817 |
| 5 | Solution Architect | 24/194 | 12.371 | [7.732, 17.010] | [8.456, 17.748] | [7.732, 17.010] | 2.380 |
| 6 | Requirements Engineer | 20/194 | 10.309 | [6.186, 14.948] | [6.773, 15.387] | [6.186, 14.948] | 2.186 |
| 7 | *Others (free text)* | 19/194 | *9.794* | *[5.670, 13.918]* | — | — | 2.123 |
| 8 | Tester | 2/194 | 1.031 | [0.000, 2.577] | [0.283, 3.680] | [0.000, 2.577] | 0.725 |

Wilson and BCa agree with the percentile intervals to ≲1 pp, so the CIs are not method artefacts. "Others" is excluded from the named-role ranking; its 19 free texts (Director, Product Owner ×3, ML Engineer, Tech Leads, SME, CEO, System Engineer, "No one", etc.) are footnoted in the script output.

## 2. Is the top-two claim significant, and is the *order* significant?
- **Top two: 100.00% of 20,000 replicates** place Project Lead/PM and Data Scientist as ranks 1–2. They separate from Business Analyst by ~23 pp, so the pair is unambiguous.
- **Order within the pair: not separable.** Paired contrast PL − DS = **+2.062 pp**, bootstrap 95% CI **[−7.732, +11.856]** (includes 0); discordant pairs 47 PL-only vs 43 DS-only; McNemar exact p = **0.752**; P(PL > DS) = 64.5%. So the data support "these two roles, jointly and clearly ahead of the rest" but **not** which of the two is first.

## 3. Denominator sensitivity (A–E) — the honest answer to the denominator ambiguity

| specification | n | ProjLead | DataSci | BusAnalyst | Developer | SolArch | ReqEng | Tester |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A all rows, −77 = not associated | 276 | 35.870 | 34.420 | 18.116 | 13.406 | 8.696 | 7.246 | 0.725 |
| **B PRIMARY: valid Q8** | **194** | **51.031** | **48.969** | 25.773 | 19.072 | 12.371 | 10.309 | 1.031 |
| C valid Q8 & Status=Completed* | 188 | 51.064 | 49.468 | 26.596 | 19.681 | 12.766 | 10.106 | 1.064 |
| D valid Q8 & D4_Role reported | 180 | 54.444 | 52.222 | 27.222 | 20.556 | 13.333 | 11.111 | 1.111 |
| E (suppl.) valid Q8 & quoted ≥1 role | 173 | 57.225 | 54.913 | 28.902 | 21.387 | 13.873 | 11.561 | 1.156 |

Ranking is **invariant across A–E**: Project Lead/PM > Data Scientist ≫ Business Analyst. Absolute levels move 35.9%→57.2% purely by denominator choice — the dominant lever, and the reason a single quoted percentage is not portable.

## 4. Cell-level diagnostic (bounded, per your instruction)
Pooled respondent × role cells: 194 × 8 = 1,552 cells, 346 quoted, p = 22.294%; iid-cell bootstrap CI [20.232, 24.420] → half-width **2.094 pp**; per-role iid-cell resampling gives the *same* ±7.2 pp as the respondent-level CI (each role is its own column of n = 194). The task's CIs imply effective n ≈ **66,154** and **48,453**; the largest defensible unit in this file is 25,538 binary cells file-wide, whose best-case half-width at p = 0.5 is 0.613 pp. **Verdict: no unit of analysis available here yields the quoted ±0.4 pp CIs, and no Q8 role reaches 61.389% (max 57.23%).** Stopping as instructed. (For completeness, the only unrelated near-hits in the file are Q11_Data_Quality 61.34% and Q9_Interviews 50.0% — different questions, not an answer to the role question.)

## 5. Secondary lens (D4_Role, not the headline)
Self-attribution is salient: 74.6% of Data Scientists name Data Scientist; 62.5% of Project Leads name Project Lead; 77.3% of Developers name Developer — evidence of in-group attribution bias, which is a reason the Q8 block (org-level attribution by all respondents) is the right headline basis. Requirements Engineer (n=2) and Tester (n=2) groups are uninterpretable.

## Limitations
1. **Break-off exclusion (82/276, 29.7%).** Missingness is block-level and all-or-nothing; all 82 are Suspended with Duration ≈ 0, so it is closer to MCAR-than-MCAR-on-topics, but it is a 30% reduction and spec A vs B differs by 15 pp. If the true target used all 276, every percentage shifts down by ~1/3.
2. **21 respondents (10.8% of 194) answered Q8 but named no role.** They are retained in the primary denominator (a genuine "nobody" signal); conditioning on naming someone (spec E) inflates all roles ~6 pp without changing the ranking.
3. **Q8 wording ambiguity.** The codebook says "degree to which **ML aspects** are addressed by <role>", while the task asks about **requirements** association. The "quoted"/"not quoted" multi-select cannot distinguish the two, so the headline statistic may measure broader ML-ownership rather than requirements ownership specifically. Q8 also has no "I don't know" option, so no refusal category is being silently collapsed.
4. **No precision on the order of the top two** (McNemar p = 0.752); any claim that Project Lead *exceeds* Data Scientist is not supported by this sample.
5. Reported percentages cannot be reconciled with the task's 61.389% at n ≤ 276; no filters were tuned to reach it.

Artifacts: executed script (deterministic — byte-identical output across two reruns) plus its saved console output and three CSV tables.

payload.hypothesis: The two roles are Project Lead / Project Manager and Data Scientist. In the survey's Q8 multi-select block (which records, role by role, whether a respondent's organization involves that role in addressing requirements/ML aspects), 99 of the 194 respondents who answered the block (51.031%, bootstrap 95% CI [43.81, 58.25]) named the Project Lead / Project Manager and 95 (48.969%, 95% CI [41.75, 56.19]) named the Data Scientist, with negative sentinels (-77/-99/-66/-1) treated as non-response. These two are far and away the most frequently associated roles: the third-ranked role, Business Analyst, is named by only 25.773% (95% CI [19.59, 31.96]), followed by Developer (19.072%), Solution Architect (12.371%), Requirements Engineer (10.309%) and Tester (1.031%). The pairing of the two leaders is robust - 100% of 20,000 respondent-level bootstrap replicates place Project Lead and Data Scientist as the top two, and their order is invariant across every denominator convention tested (all 276 rows: 35.87%/34.42%; 194 valid respondents: 51.03%/48.97%; completed-only 188: 51.06%/49.47%; role-reported 180: 54.44%/52.22%; respondents naming >=1 role 173: 57.23%/54.91%). The two are, however, statistically indistinguishable from each other (paired difference +2.06 pp, 95% CI [-7.73, +11.86]; McNemar exact p = 0.752), so the defensible claim is that these two roles jointly lead, not that one exceeds the other. Interpretation: responsibility for requirements in ML-enabled systems is concentrated in the project-management and data-science functions rather than in traditional requirements-engineering or testing roles - Requirements Engineer is named by only ~10% and Tester by ~1% - which suggests a requirements-ownership gap in ML-enabled system projects. Caveat: the ~49.6% figure is consistent with the Data Scientist proportion measured here, but the ~61.389% figure is not reproducible from this file (no role exceeds 57.23% under any defensible denominator), and the cited CI half-widths of +/-0.4 pp imply an effective sample of ~48,000-66,000 whereas this file has 276 respondents (1,552 respondent-role cells); honest respondent-level CIs are +/-7 pp.
payload.workflow: Loaded the CSV with dtype=str/keep_default_na=False to preserve sentinel tokens; coerced -77/-99/-66/-1 (and literal '0' in categorical columns) to missing; defined association as Q8_ML_Addressing_<Role> == 'quoted'; restricted to the 194 respondents with a complete non-sentinel Q8 block (primary denominator); estimated per-role proportions with a respondent-level cluster bootstrap that resamples each respondent's whole 8-role vector (B=20,000, seed=20241025, percentile 95% CI), cross-checked with Wilson and jackknife-based BCa intervals; computed the paired Project Lead minus Data Scientist contrast from the same replicate index plus an exact McNemar test on discordant pairs; measured rank stability across replicates; repeated the point estimates under denominator specifications A-E; used D4_Role only as a descriptive secondary lens; and ran a bounded cell-level (respondent x role) unit-of-analysis diagnostic to test whether the task's sub-1 pp CI widths could arise from any unit available in the file. Verified determinism by re-running the script twice and diffing the saved output.
